summary: A Victorian keeper's house and tower on a blasted rock in San Pablo Strait, lit in 1874, saved from demolition in 1971 and now a lighthouse inn.

access.note: Reached only by the inn's boat from Point San Pablo Yacht Harbor; overnight stays and summer Saturday day visits.

stay.note: Five rooms; dinner and breakfast included.

notes_for_editor: No contemporary Light-House Board reports for 1873-1878 are in the corpus, so the build account rests on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased) and the 1970 NRHP nomination; get the 1873/1874 reports. Chronicling America search returned nothing. Appropriation ($20,000 vs $30,000) and the post-1906 lens (Paris replacement per NRHP vs 1912 lens per LighthouseFriends) conflict. 1893/1894 fog-signal figures are matched to years by order within the bound 1893-94 volume (scan 229 and 546); printed pages unconfirmed. The 1898-1923 Bulletin index lists a storm-damage item (p.213) not read. Roster mismatches: LighthouseFriends starts Quinlan 1887, Wheeler/Schneyer/Brien 1950s-60s omitted from JSON roster (post-1945 USLHS lines; recent people not named). Several first-assistant 1918-1921 stints and 1945+ lines omitted for brevity should be added by editor if wanted. Story asserts NRHP date 12 Feb 1971 from NPS asset 'Date Published' (the nomination's own date stamp is OCR-garbled).
